name: Temple of Heaven: an Imperial Sacrificial Altar in Beijing
description: In southeastern Beijing, the Temple of Heaven is a park-like complex begun in the early 1400s, where Ming and Qing emperors came each year to pray to Heaven for good harvests. Its blue-roofed, round halls and altars stand among old pine woods and gardens. The layout reflects the Chinese view of earth and heaven, with the emperor as the link between them.
